newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police finish Israeli government corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Police finish Israeli government corruption probe.

text.p: Israeli police said on Tuesday they had completed a 12-week inquiry into alleged corruption in the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

An announcement said police compiled a 995-page report based on 60 depositions. Prosecutors, who will determine whether to bring any charges, will also decide when and how to make public the findings, police said.
"The investigation has reached an end after 12 weeks during which 60 depositions were taken," police said.

"Based on the opinion of the prosecution, police have decided to avoid publishing the findings and conclusions and...the prosecution will decide on the nature and timing for bringing the inquiry before the public."

Police have been looking into the cabinet's appointment last January of an attorney general. Israel's Channel One Television has alleged a Netanyahu ally on trial pushed candidate Roni Bar-On for the job in hopes of winning a plea bargain.

Suspicions have been focused on two to three figures close to Netanyahu who deny any wrongdoing, including the man on trial, Aryeh Deri of the religious Shas party. Bar-On himself quit hours after being appointed amid criticism he was professionally unfit for the job.
